To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LibriSpeech is a good training set for acoustic models, that it is not as good as WSJ for building language models, and that it is a very good set to evaluate the performance of ASR systems.

(1) the LibriSpeech corpus can be used for training acoustic models for ASR, (2) acoustic models trained on the LibriSpeech can achieve lower error rate on Wall Street Journal test sets, (3) acoustic models trained with the LibriSpeech achieve lower word error rate on the LibriVocx corpus, (4) acoustic models trained using the LibriSpeech perform better than the same models trained using a smaller subset of the LibriSpeech,

(a) LibriSpeech is a new corpus of 1000 hours, derived from Librivox audiobooks; (b) acoustic models trained on it outperform models trained on WSJs, and (c) we have made it freely available, together with scripts to train models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
building a large corpus of read English, and making it easily available for research in speech recognition.
the question of how to best leverage the large quantities of audio data that are now available in the public domain.
the question of whether the speech recognition community can take advantage of the huge amounts of speech that are available for free on the internet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LibriSpeech is a high-quality, freely available corpus that can be used to train state-of-the-art speech recognition systems.
the paper presents a new corpus of speech, and shows that it can be used to build ASR systems that are better than those trained on WSJ.
the LibriSpeech corpus provides a large, high quality training set for acoustic models, and is also suitable for evaluating language models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LibriSpeech corpus and the associated tools provide the ASR community with an easy way to train and evaluate systems that perform well on the WSJ test sets, and also provide a large corpus of read speech suitable for training and evaluation of ASR systems for read speech.
LibriSpeech is a large corpus that can be used to train ASR models that are competitive with the state-of-the-art.
Librispeech is a new large scale corpus of read speech that can be used for training and evaluation of ASR systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot to be gained by using large amounts of public domain audio data to build ASR systems.
there are large amounts of high-quality public domain speech available, and that these can be used to train high-quality acoustic models for speech recognition systems.
the LibriSpeech corpus provides a good starting point for training acoustic models for speech recognition.
